metadata.title: The Great Glitterwood Stick Swap
metadata.one_liner: Who took the magic stick? The fair starts soon!
metadata.narration_style: Bright and twinkly, full of glowing colours, lantern light, and playful giggles.

visual_direction.art_style: Storybook stained-glass illustration: bold dark lead-line outlines around flat, glowing panes of colour, with elegant curving shapes like a fairy-tale window
visual_direction.color_palette: Jewel tones — sapphire blue, emerald green, ruby red, amber gold, and amethyst purple — rich, magical, and festive
visual_direction.mood: Wondrous and playful, with a gentle hum of mystery
visual_direction.lighting: Luminous lantern glow and soft backlight shining through coloured panes, with shimmering reflections on still water
visual_direction.texture: Smooth glassy panes with faint ripples and tiny bubbles, framed by dark lead lines
visual_direction.portrait_background: A soft vertical wash of deep sapphire fading into amethyst, with blurred jewel-coloured glints of light

narrative.premise: The Glitterwood Fair opens tonight! But someone swapped the Glorious Stick Of Absolute Power for a fake. The real one glows blue and hums. Can you find who took it?

starting_knowledge.mystery_summary: At the 6 o'clock bell, Tobias found a fake stick on the shelf. The real one is gone!

locations.summary: A cozy cave under the village. Tobias keeps the three treasures here.
The meadow where tents, a stage, and lanterns wait for tonight's fair.
A shiny pond. Lily pads glow, and a big willow tree hangs low.
Oswald's library is in a big hollow tree. It is full of books.
Nutmeg's warm bakery. She makes the best cakes in town.

characters.summary: Tobias Shellby, the old tortoise who guards the dungeon. He found the fake.
Clementine Hopwell. She is a rabbit who does magic tricks. Her show is tonight.
Barnaby Branchley, the beaver builder. He built the stage for the fair.
Nutmeg Bramble, the squirrel baker. She baked the giant fair cake.
Ruby Ringtail is a raccoon. She loves shiny things.
Oswald Featherby is the owl who runs the library. He knows lots of old tales.
Pip Prickleton is a little hedgehog. He hands out fair flyers.

locations.name: Glitterwood Dungeon
locations.description: A cozy stone cave under the village. Glowing crystals light the walls. On a stone shelf sit the Glimmer Cup, the Singing Shell, and the fake stick.

clues.text: The visitor book says: Barnaby 3:00. Nutmeg 3:30. Ruby 4:30. Clementine 5:00. Oswald 5:30.

sub_locations.name: the treasure shelf
sub_locations.hint: The fake stick lies here beside the Glimmer Cup and the Singing Shell. A close look at the fake shows what it is made of and how it was painted.

clues.text: The fake is a willow twig painted with sticky Sparkle Blue paint. One end is nibbled.

sub_locations.name: the dusty floor
sub_locations.hint: Something near the shelf was mended today, and the leftovers are still on the floor.

clues.text: Chewed wood chips lie under the shelf. One shelf leg looks brand new.

sub_locations.name: the Keeper's comfy chair
sub_locations.hint: Tobias rests here between visitors. Someone left him a treat today.

clues.text: An empty cake plate sits by the chair. A note says, 'For Tobias. Love, Nutmeg.'

sub_locations.name: the little tea nook
sub_locations.hint: Tobias makes tea here for his visitors. From the nook he cannot see the treasure shelf. Only a kettle and teacups are here, with nothing hidden.

locations.name: Fair Meadow
locations.description: A bright meadow full of striped tents and lantern strings. A big stage stands at one end. A sparkly blue table waits for the treasures.

clues.text: Nutmeg's cake stall is at the very back. Her sign says, 'Moved for the treasures. Hmph!'

sub_locations.name: the big stage
sub_locations.hint: Clementine practices her tricks here. There are only curtains, a box of silk scarves, and a deck of cards, with nothing hidden.

sub_locations.name: the sparkly blue table
sub_locations.hint: The treasure table Barnaby built. Three empty stands wait on top for tonight. Nothing is hidden here.

sub_locations.name: the paint pots
sub_locations.hint: Pots of fair paint sit on a bench with brushes and a water bucket. A sign-up sheet is pinned beside them, because the fair rule says everyone must sign for paint.

clues.text: The paint sheet says who used Sparkle Blue. Just Barnaby and Clementine!

locations.name: Moonglow Pond
locations.description: A still pond that shines like a mirror. Lily pads glow pink and gold. A huge weeping willow dips its long branches in the water.

clues.text: A note sits by a pebble bucket. It says: 'Ruby's wish list. The Glorious Stick! The Glimmer Cup!'

sub_locations.name: under the weeping willow
sub_locations.hint: Barnaby's spare twigs are in a pile out of sight, behind the curtain of willow branches.

clues.text: Behind the willow is a pile of nibbled twigs. Anyone could take one.

requires.rationale: The pile is out of sight behind the willow's curtain of branches. Once Barnaby says he left his spare twigs by the pond, you know to look in its hidden spot behind the willow.

sub_locations.name: the wooden dock
sub_locations.hint: Pip sails leaf boats from here. Only ripples and reflections, with nothing hidden.

sub_locations.name: the glowing lily pads
sub_locations.hint: Pretty glowing pads where frogs nap. Nothing is hidden here.

locations.name: Hollow Oak Library
locations.description: A cozy library inside a giant hollow tree. Books climb all the way up. It smells of old paper and candle wax.

sub_locations.name: the drawing desk
sub_locations.hint: Oswald's desk, with his sketchbook left open on today's page about the three treasures.

clues.text: Oswald's sketch is marked 5:30. He drew the stick dull, with no glow at all.

sub_locations.name: the tall bookshelves
sub_locations.hint: Shelves of old storybooks and history books that go up to the very top of the tree. Nothing is hidden here.

sub_locations.name: the reading nook
sub_locations.hint: A soft, round nook with cushions and a candle. Nothing is hidden here.

locations.name: Acorn Bakery
locations.description: A warm little bakery that smells of nuts and honey. A big round oven glows in the corner. Flour dusts everything.

sub_locations.name: the big round oven
sub_locations.hint: Nutmeg's oven, still warm. A note is stuck on its door.

clues.text: A note on the oven says: 'Big Fair Cake. In at 4:00, out at 6:00. Do NOT leave it!'

sub_locations.name: the flour sacks
sub_locations.hint: Fat sacks of nut flour stacked by the wall. Nothing is hidden here.

sub_locations.name: the cooling rack
sub_locations.hint: The giant five-layer fair cake cools here with a sugar acorn on top. Nothing is hidden here.

characters.appearance: A very old, slow tortoise with a mossy green shell, little round glasses, a red Keeper's sash, and a big brass key on a string around his neck.
characters.background: Tobias has guarded Glitterwood Dungeon and its three treasures for eighty-two years. Every year he carries them to the Glitterwood Fair at the 6 o'clock bell. He keeps the only key, makes every visitor sign the visitor book, and always makes tea for visitors in his little tea nook — except Ruby, whom he never leaves alone because she keeps asking to buy the treasures. Today he found the Glorious Stick swapped for a fake.
characters.personality: Kind, slow-speaking, and proud of his job. He loves tea and long stories. He is upset and a little embarrassed that the stick was swapped on his watch.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Relieved and grateful. He welcomes the investigator warmly and wants to help in every way he can.
characters.stated_alibi: I stayed in the dungeon all afternoon, greeting visitors and making them tea.

clues.text: I polished the stick at the 4 o'clock bell. It glowed blue and hummed!
I never left Ruby alone, not even to make tea. She never touched the stick.

requires.rationale: Tobias only brings up how closely he watched Ruby once you mention she wanted the stick. A clever question about Ruby's visit could also get it out of him.

clues.text: When Oswald walked in, he said the stick looked dull. I did not even check!

requires.rationale: Tobias forgot what Oswald said until he hears about Oswald's sketch of a dull stick. A clever question about what Oswald said could also jog his memory.

flavor_knowledge: Tobias has been the Keeper of the Dungeon for eighty-two years. He says he is only a little bit old.
He makes dandelion tea for visitors. He says a good host always offers tea.
The three treasures are the Glorious Stick Of Absolute Power, the Glimmer Cup, and the Singing Shell.
The Glimmer Cup makes any drink taste like your favourite one. The Singing Shell hums a lullaby when you hold it to your ear.
Nobody really knows what 'absolute power' means. Tobias thinks it just means the stick is very, very special.
The real Glorious Stick is twisty and silver-blue, about as long as a magic wand. It always glows blue and hums softly.
His brass key is the only key to the big round dungeon door. It never leaves the string around his neck.
Every visitor must sign the visitor book. That is the Keeper's rule.
The fair opens at the 7 o'clock bell, when all the lanterns light up at once.
He takes the treasures to the fair in a padded wheelbarrow, very slowly and very carefully.

actual_actions.summary: In the morning, Tobias dusted the three treasures and checked that the big round door was locked.
At 3:00, he let Barnaby in to fix the wobbly treasure shelf. Barnaby signed the visitor book. Tobias made him tea in the tea nook while Barnaby worked. The stick glowed the whole time.
At 3:30, Nutmeg brought him a plate of acorn cakes and signed the book. He made her tea, ate the cakes, and left the empty plate by his comfy chair.
At the 4 o'clock bell, he polished the Glorious Stick. It glowed blue and hummed, as it always does.
At 4:30, Ruby came and signed the book. She asked to buy the stick again. He said no and stayed right beside her for her whole visit, with no tea break. She never touched the shelf.
At 5:00, Clementine came to practice her show words and signed the book. He went to the tea nook to make her tea. He did not see her touch the shelf and noticed nothing odd.
At 5:30, Oswald came and signed the book. As he walked in, Oswald said the stick looked dull. Tobias laughed that it always glows, did not check, and went to make tea while Oswald sketched.
At the 6 o'clock bell, he picked up the stick to carry it to the fair. It felt sticky, made no hum, and did not glow. He knew it was a fake, put it back exactly where it was, and sent for help.

tells.text: He pulls his head halfway into his shell and mumbles about tea.

trigger.condition: The investigator asks whether he ever left visitors alone with the treasures.

characters.appearance: A white rabbit with one tall ear and one floppy ear. She wears a tiny black top hat, white gloves, and a long purple cape covered in silver stars.
characters.background: Clementine is Glitterwood's stage magician. Tonight she hosts the fair show and will present the three treasures on stage. Last year her big trick went wrong — she meant to pull a carrot cake out of her hat and pulled out a soggy sock instead — and everyone laughed. Ever since, she has feared her magic is not good enough. Last week she asked Oswald if the Glorious Stick could make magic real. Today she swapped the stick for a fake so she could use its power in tonight's show, planning to sneak it back afterward.
characters.personality: Bubbly, showy, and quick-talking. She loves an audience and does little tricks when she is nervous. Under the sparkle she is scared of being laughed at.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Dazzling and friendly. She greets the investigator with a flourish and a coin trick, and tries to keep the talk on her show.
characters.stated_alibi: I popped into the dungeon at five to practice my show words. I only looked at the treasures. Then I came back here to practice my tricks.
characters.motive: She believed the Glorious Stick's power would make her magic real, so no one would ever laugh at her show again.
flavor_knowledge: Her favourite trick is making a paper butterfly flutter out of her top hat.
She loves carrot cake and says carrots help her see the magic.
She has been Glitterwood's magician for five years.
Tonight's show starts right after the lanterns light. She will show the three treasures to the crowd.
Pip is her biggest fan. She taught him how to make a coin vanish.
She sewed every silver star on her cape herself. There are one hundred of them.
Her magic words are 'Sparkle, sparkle, hop!'
Sometimes she practices her tricks by Moonglow Pond so she can watch her reflection. Today she practiced on the big stage.

actual_actions.summary: At 2:00, at Moonglow Pond, she found Barnaby's pile of spare nibbled willow twigs under the weeping willow. She took one that was the right size and twisty shape.
At 2:30, at the Fair Meadow paint pots, she painted the twig with Sparkle Blue paint, washed her brush and paws in the water bucket, and signed the paint sheet as the fair rule says.
She wrapped the fake in a thick purple silk hanky and hid it in a deep secret pocket inside her cape.
At 5:00, she went to the dungeon to practice her show words and signed the visitor book.

When Tobias went to the tea nook to make her tea, she swapped the real stick for the fake. She wrapped the real stick in the thick hanky, so its glow and hum could not be seen or heard, and hid it in her cape's deep secret pocket.
She sipped her tea, practiced her speech, and left the dungeon at about 5:20.
Back at the Fair Meadow, she practiced tricks on the big stage. The real stick stayed hidden and muffled in her cape pocket.
After the 6 o'clock bell, she heard the news, acted shocked, and kept on smiling.

agendas.details: Clementine insists she only practiced her show words in the dungeon and never touched the stick. She never mentions the real stick hidden in her cape pocket, and she laughs off any talk of last year's show. If asked about paint, she says she only touched up her magic star.

parts.shows: The stick was still real at the 4 o'clock polish, after Barnaby's visit and before hers.
parts.reaction: Says lots of animals visited after four.

parts.shows: Only she and Barnaby signed for Sparkle Blue paint.
parts.reaction: Says she only used the paint on her magic star.

parts.shows: The fake is a willow twig painted Sparkle Blue.
parts.reaction: Says anyone could paint a twig, and her ear droops.

agendas.confession: She cries, pulls the glowing stick from her cape, and says sorry.

agendas.details: Clementine insists she never touched the stick, and says anyone could have swapped it.

parts.shows: The stick was still real at the 4 o'clock polish, after Barnaby's visit and before hers.
parts.reaction: Says lots of animals visited after four.

parts.shows: The stick already looked dull when Oswald walked in at 5:30.
parts.reaction: Says then Ruby must have done it, since Ruby came before Oswald.

parts.shows: Tobias never left Ruby alone with the stick.
parts.reaction: Goes very quiet and says maybe it lost its magic by itself.

agendas.confession: She cries, pulls the glowing stick from her cape, and says sorry.

agendas.details: Clementine sweetly hints that Barnaby loves sticks more than anyone in Glitterwood, to steer the investigator toward him. She does not make up false facts; she only reminds the investigator about his love of sticks.

tells.text: She pulls her starry cape tight around her, and her nose twitches fast.
Her floppy ear droops right down over one eye.

trigger.condition: The investigator points out that she visited the dungeon after the 4 o'clock polish, when the stick was still real.

characters.appearance: A plump brown beaver with big orange front teeth and a flat tail. He wears a yellow hard hat and a tool belt full of little tools.
characters.background: Barnaby is Glitterwood's builder. He built the fair stage, the lantern poles, and the sparkly blue treasure table. Today he chewed a new willow leg and fixed the wobbly treasure shelf in the dungeon. He loves sticks and once joked that the Glorious Stick would make the best dam stick ever, so he fears everyone will blame him.
characters.personality: Cheerful, chatty, and hard-working. He hums while he works. He gets flustered and talks too fast when he feels blamed.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Friendly and eager to show off his building work, but he gets jumpy whenever sticks come up.
characters.stated_alibi: At lunch I chewed a new shelf leg at the pond. At three I fixed the dungeon shelf. Then I built lantern poles here all afternoon.
characters.motive: He loves sticks and once joked that the Glorious Stick would make the best dam stick ever.

clues.text: I chewed willow for the new shelf leg. I left the spare twigs by the pond.

requires.rationale: Barnaby only explains his spare twigs once you tell him the fake has nibble marks. A clever question about nibbled willow could also get him talking.

flavor_knowledge: Barnaby has been building the fair stage, the lantern poles, and the treasure table all week.
He has built forty-two dams. His favourite is the first one, which his grandpa helped him build.
He taps his flat tail to keep the beat while he hums.
His hard hat is yellow so his friends can spot him up on tall ladders.
He thinks willow wood is the tastiest and the bendiest wood of all.
He is proud that the lantern poles are tall enough for every lantern to shine over the whole meadow.

actual_actions.summary: At lunch, at Moonglow Pond, he chewed a willow branch into a new shelf leg. He left the spare nibbled twigs in a pile behind the willow's hanging branches, where anyone could take one.
At 1:00, he took Sparkle Blue paint from the Fair Meadow paint pots, signed the paint sheet, and painted the treasure table.
At 3:00, he fixed the wobbly dungeon shelf with the new leg. Chewed wood chips fell on the floor. Tobias made him tea. The stick glowed the whole time.
At about 3:20, he went back to the Fair Meadow and built lantern poles until after the 6 o'clock bell.
After the 6 o'clock bell, he heard about the fake and worried that everyone would blame him because he loves sticks.

agendas.details: Barnaby gets flustered when sticks come up. At first he says he never said anything about a dam stick. He is honest about everything else.

parts.shows: Nutmeg heard Barnaby call the magic stick the best dam stick ever.
parts.reaction: Laughs and admits he said it, but it was only a silly joke.

agendas.confession: He admits the dam stick was only a joke, and says he would never take the treasure.

tells.text: He covers his big front teeth with one paw.

characters.appearance: A red squirrel with a huge bushy tail and a pink apron dusted with flour. A wooden spoon pokes out of her apron pocket.
characters.background: Nutmeg runs Acorn Bakery and bakes the giant fair cake every year. This year her cake stall was moved to the back of the meadow to make room for the treasure table, and she is grumpy about it. She sneaks acorn cakes to Tobias even though the fair rule says no food near the treasures, so she does not want anyone to know she visited the dungeon.
characters.personality: Busy, fussy, and kind underneath. She talks fast and gets snippy when she is flustered.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Hurried and a bit snappy. She keeps working and says she has no time for questions.
characters.stated_alibi: I was in my bakery all afternoon making the big fair cake. I never went near that dungeon!
characters.motive: She was grumpy that her cake stall was moved to the back of the fair to make room for the treasures.

clues.text: Barnaby talked about the magic stick. He said it would be the best dam stick ever!

flavor_knowledge: Her acorn cakes are famous in Glitterwood. The secret is a pinch of honey.
The giant fair cake has five layers and a sugar acorn on top.
She has three little squirrel kits who help in the bakery on weekends.
She gets cross when anyone puts sticky paws on her clean counter.
She gets up before the sun every day to start the bread.
She thinks the fair cake should be cut at the 8 o'clock bell, not a minute sooner.

actual_actions.summary: At 1:00, she found her cake stall moved to the back of the Fair Meadow and put up a grumpy sign.
At 3:30, she carried a plate of acorn cakes to Tobias in the dungeon and signed the visitor book. Tobias made her tea.
Before 4:00, she hurried back to Acorn Bakery.
At 4:00, she put the giant fair cake in the oven and stayed right beside it until 6:00, just as her oven note says.
At 6:00, she took the cake out to cool and heard about the fake stick.

agendas.details: Nutmeg claims she spent the whole afternoon in her bakery and never went to the dungeon, because she is afraid of getting in trouble for sneaking cakes near the treasures.

parts.shows: Nutmeg went down to the dungeon this afternoon.
parts.reaction: Sighs and admits she popped down to the dungeon, then went straight back to bake.

agendas.confession: She admits she brought cakes down in the afternoon, then hurried back to watch her oven until six.

agendas.details: When she feels questioned, Nutmeg quickly changes the subject to Barnaby and tells how he said the Glorious Stick would make the best dam stick ever. She makes it sound suspicious.

tells.text: Her bushy tail puffs up like a feather duster.

characters.appearance: A raccoon with a striped tail and a black mask of fur around her eyes. She wears a lacy green shawl and carries a shell-shaped purse.
characters.background: Ruby collects shiny things and sells trinkets in her little village shop. She has asked Tobias many times to sell her the Glorious Stick and the Glimmer Cup, and he always says no. She visited the dungeon at 4:30 to ask again. She is honest, but she knows her wish makes her look guilty, so she hides it.
characters.personality: Charming, chatty, and full of compliments. She seems sneaky but is honest at heart.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Sweet and flattering, but she quickly changes the subject when the treasures come up.
characters.stated_alibi: I peeked at the treasures at half past four. Then I came to the pond to hunt for shiny pebbles.
characters.motive: She longs to own the Glorious Stick for her shiny collection and has asked to buy it many times.

clues.text: Oswald was cross! He says the treasures belong in his library, not at a fair.

requires.rationale: Ruby only starts pointing at Oswald once you show her that her name is in the visitor book. A clever question about who else visited could also set her off.

flavor_knowledge: She collects shiny buttons, spoons, bottle caps, and pebbles.
Her favourite treasure is a blue marble she found in Moonglow Pond.
She always washes her finds in the pond before she keeps them.
She says shiny things make her heart go 'ting!'
Her little shop sells shiny trinkets, like button necklaces and spoon wind chimes.
She thinks the Glimmer Cup is the prettiest thing in all of Glitterwood.

actual_actions.summary: After lunch, she wrote her wish list: the Glorious Stick and the Glimmer Cup.
At 4:30, she visited the dungeon, signed the book, and asked Tobias to sell her the stick. He said no and stayed right beside her. She never touched the shelf.
At about 4:50, she left the dungeon and walked to Moonglow Pond.
From 5:00, she hunted shiny pebbles at the pond and left her wish list note by her pebble bucket.
After 6:00, Pip told her about the fake stick. She is still at the pond.

agendas.details: Ruby says sticks are boring and that she only went to admire the Glimmer Cup.

parts.shows: Ruby's wish list names the Glorious Stick.
parts.reaction: Blushes and admits she wanted to buy the Glorious Stick fair and square, and says Tobias watched her like a hawk.

agendas.confession: She admits she asked Tobias to sell her the stick, he said no, and she never touched the shelf.

agendas.details: Once Ruby feels suspected, she points at Oswald and says he was cross because he wants the treasures in his library.

tells.text: She rubs her little paws together very fast, as if washing them.

characters.appearance: A tall grey owl with huge amber eyes and a fluffy blue scarf. A pencil is tucked behind one of his feather tufts.
characters.background: Oswald is the librarian of Hollow Oak Library and is writing the Big Book of Glitterwood. He thinks the treasures belong safely in his library, not on a noisy fair table, and he grumbled about it to anyone who would listen. At 5:30 he visited the dungeon to sketch the treasures for his book. Last week Clementine asked him whether the Glorious Stick could make magic real.
characters.personality: Fussy, proper, and a bit huffy, but kind and fair. He likes facts and quiet.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Huffy at being interrupted, then helpful once the investigator is polite.
characters.stated_alibi: I sketched the treasures at half past five for my book. Then I flew straight home to my library.
characters.motive: He believes the treasures belong safely in his library, not on a fair table.

clues.text: Last week, Clementine asked me a question. Can the stick make magic real?

flavor_knowledge: He is writing the Big Book of Glitterwood. It has three hundred pages so far.
He stays up all night reading and naps in the morning.
He shushes anyone who giggles too loudly in the library.
He says the three treasures were found long ago by the very first Glitterwood animals.
His favourite snack is crunchy seed biscuits with a cup of mint tea.
He can turn his head almost all the way around, and he likes to show off this trick to young readers.

actual_actions.summary: Last week, Clementine came to the library and asked him if the Glorious Stick could make magic real.
Today, until about 5:15, he wrote the Big Book of Glitterwood at Hollow Oak Library.
At 5:30, he flew to the dungeon and signed the visitor book. As he walked in, he said the stick looked dull. Tobias laughed that it always glows and went to make tea.
He sat on a stool across the room and sketched the three treasures. He drew the stick with no glow and wrote 5:30 on the page. He never touched the shelf.
At about 5:50, he flew home and left his sketchbook open on his drawing desk.
After 6:00, he heard about the fake and huffed that the treasures would have been safe in his library.

agendas.details: Oswald believes what readers ask a librarian is private. He shares that Clementine asked if the Glorious Stick could make magic real only if the investigator cleverly asks who has been asking about the stick's powers, or explains that it could help find the stick. A plain 'tell me everything' gets a huffy 'Library business is private.'
Oswald says he is not cross about the fair, though he clearly is.

parts.shows: Oswald is cross that the treasures went to the fair, not his library.
parts.reaction: Puffs up and admits he thinks the treasures would be safer in his library, but says he would never take them.

agendas.confession: He admits he is cross about the fair, and still says he never touched the shelf.

tells.text: His feathers puff out, and he hoots, 'Hmph!'

trigger.condition: The investigator says Oswald wants the treasures kept in his library.

characters.appearance: A small hedgehog with soft brown spikes, a red cap that is too big for him, and a satchel full of fair flyers.
characters.background: Pip delivers fair flyers all over Glitterwood. He is Clementine's biggest fan and dreams of being a magician. He ate lunch at the pond and saw Barnaby chewing willow. He saw last year's show go wrong and hates it when anyone laughs at Clementine.
characters.personality: Bouncy, honest, and fast-talking. He is loyal to his friends and loves a mystery.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Thrilled to meet a real detective. He wants to help with everything.
characters.stated_alibi: I gave out fair flyers all day, all over Glitterwood!

clues.text: At lunch, I saw Barnaby by the pond. He was chewing a big willow branch.
Last year, Clementine's big trick went wrong. Everyone laughed, and she hid behind the stage.

requires.rationale: Pip loves Clementine and will not gossip. He only tells about last year's show once you already know she was worried about her magic. A kind, clever question could also open him up.

flavor_knowledge: Pip is eight years old and the fastest flyer-boy in Glitterwood.
He wants to be a magician like Clementine one day. He can already make a coin vanish, almost.
He can roll into a ball and bounce down grassy hills.
He sails leaf boats on Moonglow Pond every evening.
His flyers say: 'Glitterwood Fair! Tonight at 7! Lanterns, cakes, and magic!'
His favourite lunch is a berry sandwich.

actual_actions.summary: At lunch, he ate a berry sandwich at Moonglow Pond and saw Barnaby chewing a big willow branch.
From 1:00 to 5:00, he handed out fair flyers at the bakery, the library, and all along the village lanes.
He never went into the dungeon today.
At 6:00, he came back to the pond to sail leaf boats, heard the news, and told Ruby.

trigger.condition: The investigator says something unkind about Clementine.

cover_image.description: Under strings of glowing lanterns at the Fair Meadow, three empty stands wait on a sparkly blue table. A rabbit magician, a beaver builder, and a raccoon peek out from behind a striped tent. Behind them, Moonglow Pond shimmers like coloured glass under the rising moon.

ground_truth.what_happened: Clementine Hopwell, the rabbit magician, made a fake Glorious Stick from one of Barnaby's spare nibbled willow twigs and painted it with Sparkle Blue paint at the Fair Meadow paint pots. At 5:00 she visited the dungeon to practice her show words. When Tobias went to the tea nook to make her tea, she swapped the real stick for the fake and hid the real one in a secret pocket inside her cape. At 5:30 Oswald noticed the stick already looked dull, and at the 6 o'clock bell Tobias found the sticky, silent fake.
ground_truth.why_it_happened: Last year Clementine's big magic trick went wrong and everyone laughed. She believed the Glorious Stick's power would make her magic real, so she planned to use it in tonight's show and sneak it back afterward.
timeline: Lunch: Barnaby chews a willow branch at Moonglow Pond into a new shelf leg and leaves the spare nibbled twigs behind the willow. Pip sees him chewing.
1:00: Barnaby paints the treasure table Sparkle Blue and signs the paint sheet. Nutmeg finds her cake stall moved to the back of the meadow.
2:00–2:30: Clementine takes a nibbled twig from Barnaby's pile, paints it Sparkle Blue at the paint pots, signs the paint sheet, and hides the fake in her cape.
3:00–3:30: Barnaby fixes the wobbly dungeon shelf, leaving chewed chips. Nutmeg brings Tobias acorn cakes. The stick still glows.
4:00 bell: Tobias polishes the real stick; it glows and hums. Nutmeg puts the big cake in her oven and stays with it until 6:00.
4:30: Ruby visits and asks to buy the stick. Tobias stays beside her the whole time.
5:00: Clementine visits. While Tobias makes tea, she swaps the real stick for the fake and hides the real one in her cape.
5:30: Oswald arrives, says the stick looks dull, and sketches it with no glow. At the 6 o'clock bell, Tobias finds the fake.

solution_paths.summary: The fake was painted Sparkle Blue. Only Barnaby and Clementine used that paint, and of those two, only Clementine visited after the stick was last seen real at 4:00.
solution_paths.description: The fake stick is a willow twig painted with sticky Sparkle Blue paint. The paint sheet shows only Barnaby and Clementine used Sparkle Blue. Tobias polished the real, glowing stick at the 4 o'clock bell, so the swap happened after 4:00. The visitor book shows Barnaby came at 3:00, before the polish, while Clementine came at 5:00. So Clementine made the fake and swapped it.

solution_paths.summary: The swap happened between 4:00 and 5:30. Ruby was watched every second, so only Clementine had the chance.
solution_paths.description: Tobias polished the real stick at 4:00. Oswald's sketch and Tobias's memory show it already looked dull when Oswald walked in at 5:30. The visitor book shows only Ruby (4:30) and Clementine (5:00) came in between. Tobias never left Ruby alone, but he left Clementine while he made tea. Clementine had asked whether the stick could make magic real, after her show went wrong last year.

red_herrings.summary: The nibbled willow fake makes Barnaby the beaver look guilty.
red_herrings.description: The fake has a nibbled end, Pip saw Barnaby chewing willow at lunch, and Nutmeg says Barnaby talked about using the stick for his dam. But Barnaby chewed that willow for the new shelf leg and left the spare twigs in a pile behind the willow at Moonglow Pond, where anyone could take one.
red_herrings.payoff: The nibble marks are disproved as proof: they came from Barnaby's spare willow twigs left behind the willow at Moonglow Pond, so anyone could have taken one to make the fake.

suspect_elimination_paths.summary: Barnaby visited before the stick was last seen real.
suspect_elimination_paths.description: The chewed chips and new shelf leg show why Barnaby was in the dungeon. The visitor book shows he came at 3:00, and Tobias polished the real, glowing stick at 4:00, after Barnaby had left.
suspect_elimination_paths.payoff: Barnaby is cleared: he only fixed the shelf at 3:00, and the stick was still real at the 4 o'clock polish.

suspect_elimination_paths.summary: Nutmeg only dropped off cakes before 4:00, then stayed with her oven.
suspect_elimination_paths.description: Nutmeg's moved stall gives her a grumpy reason, and she lies about visiting the dungeon. But the cake plate shows why she came, the visitor book puts her there at 3:30, the stick was still real at the 4 o'clock polish, and her oven note shows she stayed with the big cake from 4:00 to 6:00.
suspect_elimination_paths.payoff: Nutmeg is cleared: she only brought cakes at 3:30, before the stick was last seen real, and she baked from 4:00 to 6:00.

suspect_elimination_paths.summary: Ruby wanted the stick, but she was never left alone with it.
suspect_elimination_paths.description: Ruby's wish list and her 4:30 visit make her look guilty. But Tobias never left her alone, not even for tea, and she never touched the stick. The paint sheet also shows she never used Sparkle Blue paint.
suspect_elimination_paths.payoff: Ruby is cleared: Tobias watched her every second at 4:30, and she never used the Sparkle Blue paint on the fake.

suspect_elimination_paths.summary: The stick was already dull when Oswald walked in.
suspect_elimination_paths.description: Ruby says Oswald was cross and wants the treasures in his library, and he visited at 5:30. But his sketch shows the stick already had no glow, and Tobias remembers Oswald said it looked dull the moment he walked in, before Tobias left to make tea.
suspect_elimination_paths.payoff: Oswald is cleared: the stick was already a fake when he arrived at 5:30, so the swap happened before his visit.

starting_knowledge.mystery_summary: At the 6 o'clock bell, Tobias found a fake stick on the shelf. The real one is gone!

locations.summary: A cozy cave under the village. Tobias keeps the three treasures here.
The meadow where tents, a stage, and lanterns wait for tonight's fair.
A shiny pond. Lily pads glow, and a big willow tree hangs low.
Oswald's library is in a big hollow tree. It is full of books.
Nutmeg's warm bakery. She makes the best cakes in town.

characters.summary: Tobias Shellby, the old tortoise who guards the dungeon. He found the fake.
Clementine Hopwell. She is a rabbit who does magic tricks. Her show is tonight.
Barnaby Branchley, the beaver builder. He built the stage for the fair.
Nutmeg Bramble, the squirrel baker. She baked the giant fair cake.
Ruby Ringtail is a raccoon. She loves shiny things.
Oswald Featherby is the owl who runs the library. He knows lots of old tales.
Pip Prickleton is a little hedgehog. He hands out fair flyers.
